Job Description

Description & Requirements

AESC is looking to add a Project Manager to our team.

Full-Time
Remote

About AESC US LLC

AESC is an exciting, newly created global organization committed to solving the challenges of a sustainable future and becoming the leading supplier of full-value-chain battery solutions. Our lithium-ion batteries can be found in nearly one million electric vehicles worldwide and have a stellar safety record of zero-critical issues. AESC US is leading the way in battery technology. We design and manufacture EV battery technology for various electric vehicles and equipment. We are working hard towards unlocking the full potential of sustainable energy and climate change mitigation. We will continue to build upon our successes and expand into new markets and industries, producing innovative and competitive products and technologies that advance the goal of a zero-carbon emission future. AESC is headquartered in Japan and has battery manufacturing locations in Japan, UK, China, and the U.S.

AESC Mission

Our mission is to solve the challenges for a sustainable future. Together, we can make a meaningful impact.

About The Role

We are seeking a detail-oriented and highly organized Project Manager to support the execution of utility-scale energy storage and infrastructure projects. This role will focus on project administration, scheduling, documentation, and internal cross-team coordination to ensure smooth delivery of complex projects. The Project Manager will work closely with sales managers, engineering teams, and external stakeholders to maintain project momentum from initiation through completion.

Project Management

What You Will Do

Serve as the central point of contact for project documentation, scheduling, and reporting.
Support sales managers and project managers in tracking milestones, deliverables, and dependencies.
Coordinate internal resources and external partners to ensure timely execution of project tasks.
Maintain accurate project records, including meeting minutes, action items, and progress reports.
Assist with preparation of project proposals, RFP/RFQ responses, and client-facing documentation.
Monitor project timelines and budgets, escalating risks or delays to senior management.
Facilitate communication between cross-functional teams (engineering, procurement, sales, and services).
Support compliance with organizational standards, safety requirements, and quality assurance processes.

Technical Management

Lead remote commissioning activities for energy storage systems, including system configuration, functional testing, and performance validation.
Act as the technical authority during commissioning, guiding and directing the commissioning team to ensure successful project execution.
Perform and oversee technical service work, including troubleshooting, diagnostics, and repairs for energy storage systems.
Provide advanced technical support for service issues and collaborate with engineering teams to resolve complex challenges.
Prepare and maintain detailed commissioning and service documentation, including test reports and maintenance records.
Ensure compliance with safety standards, quality requirements, and regulatory guidelines during all commissioning and service activities.
Offer technical training and mentorship to commissioning and service team members.

Qualifications

What You Need

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Project Management, or related field (or equivalent experience).
2–4 years of project coordination, project support, or operations experience; exposure to utility-scale energy, infrastructure, or construction projects preferred.
Familiarity with project management methodologies (Agile, Waterfall, Hybrid).
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Proficiency with project management tools (MS Project, Smartsheet, Asana, Jira) and Microsoft Office.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to convey technical and commercial information clearly.
Self-driven, detail-oriented, and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment

What is “Nice to Have”?

Knowledge of energy storage systems, renewable energy, or large-scale infrastructure projects.
Understanding of permitting, interconnection, and regulatory processes.
Experience supporting EPCs, utilities, IPPs, or project developers.
Familiarity with CRM platforms and project tracking systems.

What We Offer

Welcome to AESC, supporting our state-of-the-art Gigafactories, where you'll have the opportunity to tackle the world's most fascinating challenges alongside exceptionally talented individuals who are driven to make a difference. At AESC, we offer a comprehensive compensation package. In addition, we provide a range of valuable benefits, such as 401K, and health insurance. We strive to ensure that our employees are well taken care of, enabling them to focus on their work and contribute to our collective mission of changing the world.

An inclusive and diverse work environment that fosters and encourages professional and personal development.
Highly automated, clean, safe, and temperature-controlled production environment
Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance
HSA and Flexible Spending Accounts
401K with company match
Life Insurance (Company paid and additional voluntary life available)
Paid Vacation and 14 Paid Holidays
Short term and long-term disability coverage (Company Paid)
Tuition reimbursement
Competitive base salary with performance-based incentives.
Opportunity to contribute to large-scale energy transition projects impacting grid reliability and decarbonization.
Hands-on exposure to complex, high-value infrastructure projects.
Comprehensive training in project management methodologies and energy storage technologies.
Career growth opportunities within project management, operations, or commercial functions.
Comprehensive benefits package including [health insurance, retirement plan, PTO, etc.].

Application Process

Even if you don't meet every requirement listed, if you believe this role suits you well, we encourage you to apply. Your application gives us the opportunity to learn more about you and explore potential fits within our team.

Following the submission of your application, we are committed to providing timely responses to all applicants, though response times may vary depending on the volume of submissions. If you do not receive an immediate response, please rest assured that this in no way reflects on the quality of your candidacy. Your application will be retained in our files, and we may reach out to you for future roles that align with your skills and interests. As our organization experiences rapid growth, we appreciate your patience in this process. We are actively working each day to enhance our application procedures to ensure a smoother and more efficient experience for all applicants. Thank you for your understanding and enthusiasm for joining our dynamic team.
Equal Employment Opportunity

At AESC, we are committed to providing Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) to all individuals. We participate in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S Join us in our passion to design, manufacture, and sell high-performance products, contributing to a sustainable and zero-carbon emission future.

Work Environment

The work environment is primarily an automated manufacturing plant with a concrete floor and is characterized by some temperature extremes, moderate noise, and forklift traffic. jobs.description:
Job Description

Why Join Agilent?

At Agilent, you’ll work directly with customers on high-impact laboratory projects that make a meaningful difference in their operations. You’ll gain exposure to complex, multi-site and multi-vendor environments while expanding both your technical expertise and leadership capabilities.

This role offers the opportunity to grow through a combination of hands-on field experience and increasing project ownership, all within a collaborative, customer-focused team delivering critical solutions across the life sciences industry.

Overview

Are you looking for an opportunity to apply your project management expertise and technical leadership in a highly visible, customer-facing role? Join our team and play a critical part in delivering complex laboratory projects that directly support customer success.

In this role, you will lead or support the end-to-end delivery of large, integrated laboratory service projects. This is a highly hands-on, field-based position requiring active engagement at customer laboratory sites across New England and mid-Atlantic States along with all of North America. You will work closely with internal teams, external partners, and customers to ensure solutions are delivered safely, efficiently, and to the highest quality standards.

Success in this role comes from being deeply engaged in on-site execution, coordinating real-time project activities, and adapting quickly within fast-paced, operational environments where priorities shift based on project and customer needs.

Key Responsibilities

You will contribute across the full project lifecycle, from early solution development through execution and closeout, supporting the delivery of complex, multi-vendor laboratory projects.

Key responsibilities include:

Leading on-site project execution, including vendor coordination and equipment-related activities
Monitoring progress, resolving issues in real time, and maintaining momentum across multiple project workstreams
Supporting solution design, scope development, and proposal activities
Developing and maintaining project plans (scope, schedule, budget, resources)
Coordinating with customers and stakeholders to align expectations and execution
Delivering CrossLab solutions—including laboratory relocations, consulting, and 3D lab design—while leading meetings, driving progress, maintaining documentation, and building strong relationships across customers, internal teams, and third-party vendors

What We’re Looking For

We are seeking a candidate based in Boston (MA) with a strong foundation in project management processes, tools, and best practices, complemented by hands-on experience delivering operational or facility-based projects in the field.

The ideal candidate thrives in environments where success depends on coordinating physical activities, vendor execution, and on-site decision-making. You are detail-oriented, adaptable, and capable of managing multiple priorities (multi-tasking) in dynamic, fast-paced environments.

Strong communication skills are essential, including the ability to lead meetings, provide clear updates, and maintain alignment across stakeholders.

This role is best suited for individuals who enjoy being present where the work is happening, driving progress through direct engagement with project activities at the customer site.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in a scientific or related field, or equivalent experience
5+ years of relevant professional experience, including 2+ years in customer-facing field project management
Experience applying project management methodologies
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Experience working directly with external customers
Experience with data tools/reporting systems
Experience managing equipment manufacturers and third-party service providers
Experience in busy laboratory environments, instrument service, or equipment maintenance
Ability and willingness to travel extensively (often 50%+) and spend sustained time on-site during critical project phases

Preferred Qualifications

PMP certification
Familiarity with GMP and/or GLP environments and requirements
Pharmaceutical or life sciences industry experience
Experience managing budgets (quotes, POs, invoicing)
Lean Six Sigma training or certification
Proficiency in MS Office and other software tools such as Smartsheet, SAP, or Maximo (CMMS)

Additional Details

This job has a full time weekly schedule. It includes the option to work remotely. Applications for this job will be accepted until at least November 6, 2026 or until the job is no longer posted. In the US, this position is eligible for reimbursement for personal vehicle usage.

The full-time equivalent pay range for this position is $93,760.00 - $156,755.00/yr plus eligibility for bonus, stock and benefits. Our pay ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Roboyo AI is a category shaper in Applied AI and Agentic Automation. 
We help leading enterprises move from automation projects and AI experiments into governed, production-grade systems that execute real work across workflows, processes, products and services.  
Our heritage is in scaled enterprise automation; our future is Applied AI and Agentic Automation: autonomous agents, AI engineering squads, process orchestration, data and knowledge foundations, and human-in-the-loop governance embedded deeply into how our clients operate.  
We are not here to sell AI theatre. We are here to turn AI into working systems, measurable outcomes and repeatable transformation programs.  

The Project Manager / Strategy Lead is a consulting-minded leader who shapes and delivers this engagement — running discovery and workshops, defining the AI and automation strategy with client executives, and translating it into disciplined, measurable delivery.  You will orchestrate cross-functional teams spanning Automation Engineers, AI Engineers, Data Scientists, Architects, and business stakeholders — driving delivery with rigor, managing client relationships with credibility, and navigating the complexity of an enterprise Automation and AI program with composure and clarity. The ideal candidate brings consulting experience, the structured thinking of a seasoned PM, and the contextual fluency to hold meaningful conversations with AI Architects and C-suite executives alike. 

Key Responsibilities: 

Strategy, Discovery & Program Leadership  

Lead strategy and advisory engagements for Financial Services clients — framing the business problem, shaping the AI and automation roadmap, and building the business case that secures executive sponsorship. 
Design and run discovery — stakeholder interviews, current-state process assessments, and opportunity sizing — to identify and prioritise high-value AI and automation use cases. 
Plan and facilitate client workshops (visioning, design thinking, use-case prioritisation, and future-state design) that move senior stakeholders from ambition to an agreed plan. 
Translate the strategy into governed delivery — establishing the PMO structure, governance forums, and reporting cadences. Define and manage the integrated program plan across all workstreams (RPA, Agentic Workflows,Generative AI, Data Science, Data Engineering), tracking milestones, dependencies, and critical path.   
Run project planning, reviews, and RAG with technical leads; maintain velocity metrics and remove blockers.   
Ensure all deliverables are tracked against scope, schedule, budget, and quality criteria, with proactive escalation of deviations.   
Maintain program documentation — charter, WBS, RACI, status reports, and decision logs — to the highest standards.  

Program Management 

Manage program risks, issues, dependencies, and change control, with clear ownership, mitigation plans, and timely escalation. 

Serve as the primary client contact, align business and technical stakeholders, and communicate program status, decisions, and priorities to senior leadership. 

Own resource planning, team capacity, budgets, forecasts, commercial performance, and financial risk across the program. 

Automation and AI Program Context & Digital Fluency  

This role requires a consulting-minded leader with hands-on fluency across modern AI and automation delivery — capable of holding credible, substantive conversations with AI Engineers, Architects, Data Scientists, and RPA developers on feasibility, timelines, and technical dependencies.  

Oversee delivery of intelligent automation and RPA workstreams — understanding bot lifecycle management, exception handling frameworks, orchestration platforms, and the interplay between RPA, AI, and enterprise systems.  

Understand the unique delivery dynamics of agentic AI programs — including multi-agent orchestration, tool-use design, prompt engineering cycles, and the governance considerations around autonomous decision-making systems.  

Adapt PM practices to the non-linear, iterative nature of ML and AI delivery — managing experimentation phases, data dependency risks, model validation cycles, and the transition from prototype to production.  

Act as a translator and bridge between business stakeholders who think in outcomes and technical teams who think in architectures — facilitating shared understanding and aligned decision-making across both worlds. 

Qualifications 

5-7 years of combined consulting and project / program management experience, including at least 3-5 years in a management consulting, strategy, or advisory role, and a track record of leading large-scale digital transformation, automation, or AI/ML programs. 
Demonstrated experience managing enterprise Financial Services engagements in a consulting or system integrator environment — ideally at a global technology firm.
Demonstrated ability to lead strategy and discovery work — facilitating executive workshops, structuring ambiguous problems, synthesising findings into clear recommendations and roadmaps, and building business cases.
Hands-on use of AI tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude) to speed up discovery, analysis, and deliverable creation. 
Strong understanding of AI/ML delivery lifecycles — including model development, MLOps, and LLM integration — sufficient to manage technical teams and client expectations effectively. 
Proven track record of managing cross-functional teams of 15+ people across multiple concurrent workstreams. 
Hands-on experience with Agile, Scrum, and SAFe delivery frameworks; comfortable operating in hybrid Agile-Waterfall environments. 
Experience with program financials — budget ownership, P&L tracking, and commercial/contract management. 
Exceptional communication, workshop facilitation, and executive presentation skills — able to adapt style for engineering teams, business sponsors, and C-suite audiences. 
Proficiency with delivery tooling: JIRA, Confluence, MS Project

Nice to have qualifications

Prior experience managing AI, Generative AI, or Automation based programs in a client-facing delivery context.  

Experience managing distributed offshore-onshore delivery teams across multiple time zones.  

Knowledge of pre-sales processes — ability to contribute to proposals, effort estimates, and client solution presentations.  

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Business Administration, or relevant experience; an MBA is a plus  

PMP, PRINCE2, PgMP, or equivalent program management certification is preferred; Agile certifications (SAFe SP, CSM) are a plus.

jobs.description:
About Aalyria

Aalyria is a leading technology company that supplies laser communications technology and temporospatial software-defined networking platforms to the aerospace industry. With technology acquired from Google, Aalyria is at the forefront of innovation in satellite and airborne mesh networks, as well as cislunar and deep-space communications. We are revolutionizing the orchestration and management of planetary mesh networks using any radio or optical spectrum, any orbit, and any hardware across land, sea, air, and space.

Role Overview

Aalyria's Spacetime platform orchestrates highly dynamic aerospace networks using a temporospatial Software Defined Networking (SDN) approach, managing not just routing but the physical link topology and lower-layer configuration underneath it.

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager to own execution on one of our most sensitive customer programs, work that requires an active TS/SCI clearance

, with a polygraph strongly preferred given the access levels involved. You'll be the linchpin between Aalyria's engineering teams and a cleared government customer, driving technical tradeoffs directly rather than simply tracking them. Engineering will look to you to make sequencing, scope, and architecture-adjacent calls, and to represent program status and risk with complete accuracy to customer stakeholders who may not always have full visibility into every technical detail.

This is a role for someone who can operate independently inside a classified environment, hold their own in a room with Staff or Principal engineers, and get things done through influence rather than authority.

Key Responsibilities

End-to-End Technical Program Execution: Own program planning and execution for a classified Spacetime engineering effort, driving the work through each phase of the mission and directly resolving cross-system dependencies and technical tradeoffs, not just surfacing them for others to decide.
Cleared Customer & Stakeholder Leadership: Serve as the primary programmatic interface with a cleared government customer, communicating fluently with both technical staff and senior government stakeholders across classified and unclassified channels.
Cross-Functional Orchestration: Run the operating rhythm, such as kickoffs, technical reviews, exec readouts, that keeps Engineering, Product, and Solutions Engineering aligned on status, risk, and decisions across compartmented and uncompartmented workstreams.
Requirements Translation & Technical Judgment: Translate customer and mission requirements into actionable engineering plans. You should be able to read and critique a design document unaided, and reason in real time about latency, throughput, scaling, and failure-mode tradeoffs.
Security & Compliance Stewardship: Handle classified information and CUI correctly as a matter of course, maintain a sound personal security posture, and follow program security and export-control (ITAR/EAR) requirements without needing to be reminded. Partner closely with the FSO and IT/Cybersecurity, who are direct stakeholders in how this role is evaluated.
Contract & Financial Management: Own T&M or cost-type contract reporting requirements, including monthly labor, subcontract, hardware, and materials tracking at the Master Equipment List (MEL) level to support invoicing.
Risk & Delivery Coordination: Identify schedule, scope, and dependency risk early; escalate with context; and coordinate mitigations directly with engineering leads across development, staging, and dedicated government cloud production environments.

Required Qualifications

Active TS/SCI clearance in good standing. TS/SCI with polygraph is strongly preferred given the access levels this role requires.
5+ years of experience in technical program management, engineering program management, or a closely related role delivering complex technical platforms, ideally for U.S. Government or defense/space customers.
Demonstrated technical depth: the ability to read and critique a design document unaided, and to engage engineering teams on architecture, scaling, and failure-mode tradeoffs as a peer, not a translator.
A track record with genuinely technical programs, infrastructure migrations, API/interface contracts, cross-system dependency resolution, or multi-team technical rollouts, not just cross-functional coordination with a technical flavor.
Proven ability to influence without authority and interface confidently with senior government and customer stakeholders.
Experience managing complex project financials, resource tracking, or strict contractual reporting requirements (T&M, FFP, or cost-type contracts).
U.S. citizenship (required to hold and maintain the clearance level above).
Background in engineering, hardware/software systems, or solutions architecture, or a related field with hands-on experience running technical programs alongside engineering teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Familiarity with networking, telecom, or SDN/traffic engineering concepts.
Strong background in satellite and mission operations — early-orbit commissioning, fleet readiness, or operating in high-consequence environments.
Experience supporting programs that have transitioned from prototype to production volumes, and improving TRL/MRL along the way.
In-depth knowledge of USG acquisition processes, FAR/DFARS, and contract vehicles (BAAs, sole-source, IDIQs, OTAs).
Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science, or a related technical field — preferred, not mandatory. Equivalent hands-on technical experience is evaluated on equal footing.
Willingness to travel occasionally as program needs require.

Compensation

The base salary for this role is $187,000 – $207,000, which may vary by geographic location. Compensation also includes a competitive equity grant, an annual performance bonus, and a comprehensive benefits package. Your final offer will reflect your location, skills, qualifications, and experience.

What We Offer

Innovative Environment: Work at a cutting-edge company shaping the future of aerospace communications.
Impactful Work: Directly contribute to critical national security programs and initiatives.
Growth Opportunities: Expand your career with opportunities for professional development and advancement.
Inclusive Culture: Be part of a collaborative, supportive, and inclusive workplace where your contributions matter.

CIG produces a steady volume of institutional research on digital asset managers and allocators: a monthly survey program, a quarterly outlook magazine, a monthly newsletter, co-branded research with index and data partners, and regular written commentary. Own the publishing calendar across weekly, monthly, and quarterly cadences and keep it on schedule

Run the monthly survey program end to end: questionnaire design, fielding, analysis, report production, and distribution

Produce the quarterly outlook magazine and manage co-branded research with partners

Draft and edit blog posts, commentary, and reports from conversations, notes, and internal data

Monitor manager, counterparty, and market news and flag what matters to the research team

Handle distribution: email platforms, website updates, LinkedIn and X posts, and basic design

Support events with invitations, logistics, and follow-up

Track what allocators open, read, and respond to, and report it back to the team

Over time, contribute to research beyond digital assets and to how we present portfolio work to institutional clients

Who you are

One to two years in traditional finance, ideally in research, investment analysis, or a related role at an asset manager, bank, consultant, or data provider

One to two years of crypto research, either at a firm or on your own time. Independent work counts if you can show it

Follows digital assets closely enough to talk with a manager or allocator without needing terms explained

Comfortable with data. You can build a survey, clean the results, and turn them into charts and findings

A clear writer who can take a short conversation and return a draft that sounds like the person who spoke

Genuinely curious. You read past the first paragraph and ask why

Organized and reliable on deadlines, with working knowledge of standard tools such as email platforms, Canva, and site builders

Our Culture

CIG recruits high agency self starters. You’ll take on real ownership early, with a direct line to the CEO and the tools and support you need to win. Remote. Candidates must be based in the United States and able to work during US business hours.

Compensation

Base salary of $60,000 to $80,000, depending on experience, with competitive benefits and equity.

Work authorization

Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States. We are not able to sponsor visas for this role.

Applications must be submitted by email. We will not review applications received through LinkedIn or other channels, or applications missing any of the items below.

Your resume
.
Two examples of research you have produced.

What are three trends in digital assets right now that are not making headlines but matter to anyone actively investing in the space?
